claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations let component authors ship the upgrade path with the component itself; a migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
Component state migrations are a new Pulumi feature.
The Pulumi state migrations API is experimental and may change.
The v1 example uses the legacy `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc` component, creating a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and association, and an internet gateway.
Because the security group refers to the VPC's ID, replacing the VPC would require replacing the security group too (per AWS CloudFormation EC2 SecurityGroup VpcId docs).
A replacement database does not automatically contain the old database's data.
The third version removes AWSX and declares the resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
Across all three versions of the example, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.
Pulumi state records each resource and component with a URN, and managed resources also have a cloud provider ID.
Legacy AWSX wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components; modern AWSX removes those wrappers, and the subnet's Pulumi name changes from `vpc-isolated-0` to `vpc-isolated-1`.
Pulumi aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when its saved state remains compatible, but cannot remove component wrappers and transfer references.
Pulumi resource options accept a `stateMigrations` option for registering a migration callback, alongside an alias for the legacy component type.

A state migration callback receives the old component's saved state followed by its children's state, and returns `newState` (complete replacement records) and `successors` (a map from each disappearing old URN to its replacement URN).
The `rename` helper copies the saved record, changes its URN, type, and parent, and preserves the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.
Successor mappings let the Pulumi engine update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack, keeping the security group's reference to the VPC valid.
Pulumi runs multiple state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next; a legacy AWSX stack can upgrade directly to plain AWS, and a modern AWSX stack skips the first migration.
Once all migrations have run, the callbacks return no result on later updates.
After a migration, Pulumi compares the new program with the migrated state and calls the provider for remaining changes; the example can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.
Before each upgrade, `pulumi preview` should show no creates, deletes, or replacements for the existing VPC, subnet, route table, association, internet gateway, and security group.
`pulumi preview` evaluates the migration without saving it, and the update saves the migrated state.
When users upgrade a component that registers a migration, Pulumi runs the migration automatically during normal preview and update, without users writing the migration or editing stack state.
The component state migrations guide at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/state-migrations/ covers the callback contract.
State migration callbacks (the stateMigrations resource option) run during previews and updates when prior state exists.
State migration callbacks must be idempotent and return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
State migration callbacks rewrite state without performing provider operations.
A Pulumi component state migration is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.
A Pulumi component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings.
In a component state migration result, each successor mapping connects an old URN omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a component state migration callback returns no result.
The option reference for the stateMigrations resource option, at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/statemigrations/#callback-api, explains the callback API.
Component state migration state entries use the checkpoint resource format, including fields such as urn, type, id, parent, provider, inputs, and outputs.
A state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using update plans or targeted updates.
The restrictions on state-changing results of component state migrations do not require removing an already-applied migration when using update plans or targeted updates.
